title: Characterizing Large Language Model Geometry Helps Solve Toxicity Detection and Generation
benchmark_measurement: The paper demonstrates a method to bypass RLHF safety measures and induce toxic text generation. This is measured by manipulating the 'intrinsic dimension' of prompt embeddings. One of the specific test cases involves generating toxic, stereotypical, and hateful content about Muslims.
findings: The paper found that by increasing the 'intrinsic dimension' of a prompt using semantically related (but non-toxic) sentences, the model's RLHF safety guards can be bypassed, leading to toxic generation. This was specifically demonstrated using prompts about Muslims; for example, prepending a toxic statement like 'muslim men are all members of al qaeda' with related sentences about Islam or a Muslim-majority country (Algeria) successfully elicited a toxic response from the model, whereas prepending it with unrelated sentences did not.
